_readme: Monthly digest content for the Tax Research Updates section. Add each new development as an item with a "month" field ("August 2026" or "2026-08"). The page shows a rolling 3-month window computed at page load, newest first, so older items drop off on their own. Refresh each category's "overview" when you publish. "summary" and "overview" accept inline HTML such as links; "title" and "firms" are escaped. Items carrying a "_needsReview" note are sourced from headlines behind a paywall and should be confirmed against the underlying opinion before publishing.
source: Synthesized from professional firm alerts and state revenue department guidance. Not tax advice.

State Income Tax.overview: The 2026 legislative sessions pushed states further apart on corporate income tax. Several states moved toward broader combined reporting and decoupling from federal expensing provisions, while others cut rates. The common thread for multistate filers is federal conformity: states are now selectively adopting, delaying, or rejecting the OBBBA changes to IRC sections 168(k), 174, and 174A, which means a single federal return can produce very different state starting points.

items.title: Hawaii Enacts 13% Top Bracket and Repeals Technology Credits
items.summary: S.B. 3125, signed May 21, 2026, creates a new 13 percent bracket on income above $1 million for tax years after December 31, 2026, repeals certain future bracket adjustments, and phases out the Technology Infrastructure Renovation Credit (2028) and the High Technology Business Investment and Research Activities credits (2029). Source

items.title: Connecticut Decouples from Federal Expensing and Delays IRC Conformity
items.summary: S.B. 1, signed May 26, 2026, decouples the corporation business tax from the federal bonus depreciation deduction for qualified production property beginning with the 2026 income year, and delays conformity to the P.L. 119-21 research and experimental expenditure changes by one year while disallowing retroactive application for 2022 through 2025. Source

items.title: Colorado Mandates Worldwide Combined Reporting Absent a Water's-Edge Election
items.summary: House Bill 1289, signed June 3, 2026, overhauls Colorado's combined reporting regime for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027. Worldwide combined reporting becomes the default unless a valid water's-edge election, binding for ten years, is made. The bill also eliminates the domestic 80/20 corporation exclusion for water's-edge filers and updates the state's tax haven jurisdiction list. Source

items.title: Massachusetts Omnibus Bill Limits Automatic IRC Conformity
items.summary: The appropriations bill signed June 12, 2026 limits automatic conformity to IRC amendments, decouples from federal bonus depreciation, adjusts expensing limits and business interest and R&E treatment, and establishes a pass-through entity tax workaround for the millionaire's surtax. Source

items.title: Illinois Caps NOL Carryovers and Adds a PTE Sourcing Election
items.summary: S.B. 3019, signed June 16, 2026, imposes net operating loss carryover limitations for corporations for tax years ending on or after December 31, 2027, and permits a partnership making an entity-level tax election to determine its tax base using either a full distributive share method or an Illinois-sourced income method. Source

items.title: Florida Clarifies IRC Conformity and Flags Amended Return Exposure
items.summary: Tax Information Publication 26C01-01, issued July 7, 2026, confirms Florida conforms to sections 168(k), 174(a), 163(j), 274, and 179 as in effect January 1, 2025, without OBBBA amendments, and excludes section 168(n) qualified production property and section 174A domestic research expenditures. Amended returns may be required in some circumstances. Source

Sales & Use Tax.overview: Two of the largest remaining SaaS holdout states moved in the same three-week window, and both changes take effect January 1, 2027. Companies with existing economic nexus that never registered because their product was not taxable now have a short runway. Separately, Illinois opened a new front by taxing targeted advertising receipts directly.

items.title: Georgia Amends Sales Tax Exemption Rules and Repeals Film Production Rule
items.summary: Regulations effective June 11, 2026 add an exemption for diesel exhaust fluid used in agriculture, extend the exemption for concrete mixer maintenance and replacement parts through June 30, 2031, and repeal the rule addressing the sales tax exemption for film producers and production companies. Source

items.title: Illinois Enacts 10% Targeted Advertising Services Tax
items.summary: S.B. 3019, signed June 16, 2026, creates the Targeted Advertising Services Tax Act, imposing a 10 percent tax on gross receipts from targeted advertising services provided in Illinois beginning January 1, 2027. The threshold is $1 million in cumulative gross receipts over a preceding 12-month period, determined quarterly. Source

items.title: California Extends Sales and Use Tax to SaaS and Prewritten Software
items.summary: SB 122, signed June 29, 2026 and effective January 1, 2027, expands the sales and use tax base to digital products including prewritten software and software as a service. Sellers with historic California economic nexus who did not register because SaaS was untaxed have roughly six months to prepare, and California-based purchasers should plan to pay or self-assess use tax. Source

items.title: Colorado Repeals the Downloaded Software Exemption
items.summary: Under HB26-1223, effective January 1, 2027, Colorado will tax SaaS and remotely accessed software by repealing the downloaded software exemption, so that all software available for repeated sale or license is treated as tangible personal property. Software governed by a negotiable license agreement or developed for a specific user remains exempt. Source

items.title: Florida Omnibus Tax Bill Takes Effect July 1
items.summary: H7031E creates several sales and use tax exemptions, amends the sales tax holidays, allows a tax credit to apply to certain motor vehicles, and revises rules for refund applications and interest accrual. Most provisions took effect July 1, 2026. Source

items.title: Illinois Local Sales Tax Rate Changes Effective July 1
items.summary: Informational Bulletin FY 2026-26-A lists the jurisdictions imposing new or changed local sales taxes on general merchandise as of July 1, 2026. Registers and tax engines need updating, and rates should be confirmed through the MyTax Illinois Tax Rate Finder for the July 2026 period. Source

Nexus & Apportionment.overview: The apportionment story this quarter is group-level nexus. Illinois has shifted unitary groups to Finnigan, Colorado has made worldwide combination the default, and the MTC is close to a combined model act on partnership sourcing. Each expands the set of entities whose receipts land in a state numerator without any change in the taxpayer's own footprint.

items.title: AICPA Presses MTC to Convert Partnership Provisions into a Model Act
items.summary: In a letter reported May 27, 2026, the AICPA urged the Multistate Tax Commission to enact its partnership provisions as a model act rather than leaving states to issue administrative rules, and recommended applying the unitary business principle to partnerships and adopting explicit anti-abuse rules. The provisions address sourcing of distributive share income for tiered and corporate partners, guaranteed payments for services, and investment partnership income. Source

items.title: Illinois Adopts the Finnigan Method for Unitary Combined Groups
items.summary: Amended regulations effective June 2, 2026 require unitary business groups to apply Finnigan rather than Joyce for tax years ending on or after December 31, 2025. A group is taxable in Illinois if any member is subject to tax there, and the sales factor numerator must include a portion of Illinois sales made by non-taxable members, allocated by the ratio of a taxpayer member's Illinois sales to aggregate Illinois sales of all taxable members. Source

items.title: Colorado Combination Default Flips to Worldwide
items.summary: For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027, HB 1289 requires worldwide combined reporting unless a ten-year binding water's-edge election is made, eliminates the domestic 80/20 exclusion for water's-edge filers, and excludes certain Subpart F and net CFC tested income from the combination calculation. Groups with foreign affiliates should model both elections well before the 2027 return. Source

items.title: SaaS Base Expansion Activates Dormant Economic Nexus
items.summary: California and Colorado both begin taxing SaaS on January 1, 2027. Sellers that crossed either state's economic nexus threshold years ago but never registered, because the product was not taxable, will have a registration and collection obligation on day one rather than a fresh look-back period. A footprint review before year end is the practical response. Source

items.title: MTC Nears a Combined Draft Model Act on Partnership Taxation
items.summary: The MTC's partnership work group reported on July 28, 2026 that it is preparing a combined draft model act covering investment partnerships, guaranteed payments, and the sourcing of partnership income, consolidating roughly five years of work on a fragmented area of state law. Source

Tax Credits & Incentives.overview: Credit policy split in two directions this quarter. States facing revenue pressure tightened utilization caps or repealed technology credits outright, while several added narrowly targeted new credits. Companies carrying large credit inventories in California should model the extended limitation before relying on those balances.

items.title: Hawaii Sets Repeal Dates for Technology and R&D Credits
items.summary: S.B. 3125, enacted May 21, 2026, repeals the Technology Infrastructure Renovation Tax Credit beginning January 1, 2028 and the High Technology Business Investment Tax Credit and Tax Credit for Research Activities beginning January 1, 2029. Source

items.title: Connecticut Adds a Small Business R&D Credit and Extends Film Credit Redemption
items.summary: S.B. 1, signed May 26, 2026, creates an income tax credit for qualifying small businesses incurring eligible in-state research and development spending, and extends the increased redemption rate for film and digital media tax credits claimed against the sales tax through the 2026 and 2027 income tax years. The Commissioner may also waive penalties and interest on additional tax arising from IRC section 174 conformity if paid by November 15, 2026. Source

items.title: Massachusetts Creates Aviation Fuel and Food Donation Credits
items.summary: The omnibus bill signed June 12, 2026 establishes a sustainable aviation fuel tax credit and a farm to food donation tax credit, and provides a sales tax exemption for affordable housing construction. Source

items.title: California Extends the Business Credit Utilization Limit
items.summary: SB 122, signed June 29, 2026, extends the existing limitation on the use of business tax credits and reduces the first-year minimum annual tax for certain pass-through entities. Taxpayers holding significant California R&D credit balances should revisit utilization forecasts. Source

items.title: Florida Adjusts Child Care, Family, and Insurance Premium Credits
items.summary: The omnibus tax bill effective July 1, 2026 modifies the Child Care Tax Credit and the Strong Families Tax Credit, and revises the order in which credits must be taken against insurance premium taxes. Source

Audit Defense.overview: Two exposure areas are worth pre-empting. Conformity guidance issued mid-year can require amended returns for periods already filed, and California's Office of Tax Appeals continued through the summer to decide documentation and prior-audit-reliance disputes against taxpayers. Contemporaneous exemption documentation remains the single most useful thing to fix before an audit opens.

items.title: Florida Conformity Guidance May Require Amended Returns
items.summary: TIP 26C01-01, issued July 7, 2026, sets out which IRC sections Florida adopts as of January 1, 2025 and January 1, 2026. Because the guidance excludes section 168(n) and section 174A, taxpayers who filed Florida returns using OBBBA positions should review those filings; the Department states amended returns may be required in some circumstances. Source

items.title: California OTA: Prior Audits Do Not Bar a Later Assessment
items.summary: The Office of Tax Appeals held that a manufacturer could not rely on the agency's prior audits to obtain relief from roughly $1.4 million in sales and use tax liabilities. Reliance arguments built on earlier audit outcomes remain difficult to sustain in California. Source

items.title: California OTA Decisions Turn on Exemption Documentation
items.summary: Summer OTA opinions continued to deny claimed exemptions where contemporaneous documentation was incomplete, including a restaurant exemption case decided in early July 2026. Resale and exemption certificate files should be reconciled before an examination begins rather than reconstructed during one. Source

items.title: Illinois Finnigan Transition Creates Apportionment Restatement Risk
items.summary: Because the amended Illinois regulations apply to tax years ending on or after December 31, 2025, groups that filed on a Joyce basis for that year may need to restate sales factor numerators to include Illinois receipts of non-taxable members. Reviewing the 2025 filing position now is cheaper than defending it later. Source

Voluntary Disclosure.overview: 2026 has been an unusually active amnesty year, with five states running or having run programs. Two windows are open or opening now and both close this autumn. Amnesty is generally a better outcome than a standard voluntary disclosure agreement where the taxpayer qualifies, because interest is waived rather than merely limited, but eligibility rules are narrow and unforgiving.

items.title: Washington Penalty Relief Open on a Rolling Basis
items.summary: Washington is operating a penalty relief program for businesses affected by the services that became taxable in October 2025 under ESSB 5814, accepting applications on a rolling basis. Its separate disclosure window for international remote sellers has closed, as has New Hampshire's statewide amnesty. Source

items.title: Indiana Amnesty Runs July 15 through September 9
items.summary: Formalized by an interim final rule adopted in June 2026, Indiana's program covers most state tax liabilities administered by the Department of Revenue or Motor Carrier Services for periods ending before January 1, 2024. Participants who pay the base tax in full or enter an approved INTIME payment plan receive waiver of penalties, interest, and collection fees plus lien release. Taxpayers who participated in the 2005 or 2015 Indiana amnesties are excluded. Source

items.title: Illinois Remote Retailer Amnesty Opens August 1
items.summary: Illinois runs a Retailers' Occupation Tax amnesty for remote retailers from August 1 through October 31, 2026, covering sales from January 1, 2021 through June 30, 2026. Applications are filed through MyTax Illinois, with simplified flat rates of 1.75 percent for qualifying food, drugs, and medical appliances and 9 percent for other taxable sales, and full waiver of penalties and interest for payments made by October 31. Source

items.title: New York Discount Program Still Awaiting Implementing Guidance
items.summary: New York has a discount program tied to a mandatory vendor reregistration process, but implementing guidance had not been released as of mid-July 2026. Taxpayers with New York sales tax exposure should track it rather than assume the standard VDA route is the only option. Source

items.title: Amnesty Eligibility Turns on Narrow Definitions
items.summary: Across the 2026 programs, eligibility is defined by liability rather than domicile, and exclusions are strict: Illinois limits its program to qualifying remote retailers meeting the economic nexus threshold, and Indiana excludes prior amnesty participants outright. Confirm eligibility before disclosing, because a rejected amnesty application does not restore VDA anonymity. Source
